title: We are turning Hawai'i into a target and calling it defense
body: The Intercept, running a piece by military budget analyst William Hartung, lays out what the Pentagon's China obsession actually costs. Trump and Pete Hegseth want a $1.6 trillion military budget next year. The $600 billion increase alone is almost twice China's entire annual defense budget. Much of that Pacific buildup runs through Hawai'i, which the strategy treats as a forward launching pad for a war with Beijing. That posture does one guaranteed thing. It puts a target on the islands, the same way Pearl Harbor was a target in 1941.

The bill is already due, even with the guns silent. A new Institute for Policy Studies report finds the military poisoned Hawai'i's land and water, then oversold what it gave back. The Navy's Red Hill fuel facility, which held roughly 250 million gallons of jet fuel, leaked into the drinking water of 93,000 people on Oʻahu. Cleanup at just three sites runs close to $500 million. The Pentagon overstated its economic benefit to the islands by nearly 30 percent, and Washington still owes up to $133.7 billion in back rent. Military money also buys fewer jobs than almost anything else, 5.3 per million dollars versus 12.3 for schools, food, or housing.

The man drafting the new tactical-nuke strategy, Elbridge Colby, says the US needs to prioritize a conflict with China "precisely in order to avoid it." This is the same official who could not say whether the US was at war with Iran a month into that fight. China is the top trading partner of 120 countries and has not fought a real war since 1979. The threat is real enough to sell a trillion-dollar budget and thin enough to need constant advertising. Hawai'i pays either way.
